construct: HSD11B2 encodes renal 11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2, which converts active cortisol to inactive cortisone in mineralocorticoid target cells. Loss permits cortisol to activate mineralocorticoid receptors, causing sodium retention, hypertension, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, and suppression of both renin and aldosterone.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Childhood severe hypertension with hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, low renin, low aldosterone, and biallelic HSD11B2 loss identifies apparent mineralocorticoid excess. 11-beta-HSD2 normally inactivates cortisol to cortisone in mineralocorticoid target cells.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: 11-beta-HSD1 catalyzes the opposite cortisone-to-cortisol direction in other tissues; adrenal 11-beta-hydroxylase and aldosterone synthase defects alter steroid synthesis, while the mineralocorticoid receptor itself is not constitutively active in HSD11B2 disease.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The directionality of cortisol-to-cortisone conversion is the critical key-integrity point and is directly supported by both the biochemical phenotype and HSD11B2 genotype.
